title: Unauthenticated MCP Config Disclosure → RCE in ByteDance deer-flow
summary: The MCP config API leaked env/headers/OAuth creds with no auth, and let anyone rewrite an MCP server's stdio command — turning tool init into backend RCE, and host takeover via a mounted docker.sock.

title: Unauthenticated Command Execution in NASA's AIT-GUI
summary: Four compounding weaknesses in the web front end of NASA/JPL's AMMOS Instrument Toolkit let an unauthenticated attacker relay arbitrary commands to the spacecraft command bus.

title: Path Traversal → Arbitrary File Write in Orbax P2P Checkpointing
summary: The emergency peer-to-peer checkpoint service let a network peer write files outside the staging directory on a training host — arbitrary file write on the victim machine.

title: Path Traversal in Microsoft's Container-Migration-Solution-Accelerator
summary: One innocent-looking os.path.join in a FastAPI catch-all route opened arbitrary file read on the server — up to full credential disclosure via /proc/self/environ.

title: SSTI → RCE via Unsandboxed Jinja2 in IBM's MCP Context Forge
summary: PromptService._render_template rendered user-controlled templates in a plain jinja2.Environment instead of a SandboxedEnvironment, allowing stored templates to reach __builtins__ and run OS commands.

title: OS Command Injection via Execution-Workspace cleanupCommand
summary: A cleanupCommand field on a workspace endpoint was passed straight to a shell on archive — five HTTP requests turn into remote code execution as the server process.

title: Hardening aiohttp's CookieJar.load() Against Unsafe Deserialization
summary: CookieJar.load() deserialized data without validation. Reported by tsigouris007; I authored the upstream remediation (commit dcf40f3) shipped in aiohttp 3.14.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery in pydantic-ai URL Download
summary: download_item() fetched user-supplied URLs with no validation, letting attacker-controlled message history reach 169.254.169.254 and internal services — cloud-metadata credential theft via chat.

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data in NVIDIA TensorRT
summary: A deserialization flaw in TensorRT lets a crafted input trigger unsafe object loading, with potential for code execution on the host running the engine.
